successors.note: Matches the 1391 gain in duchy-of-cleves. The page then has the Mark go to Brandenburg in 1614 ('Treaty of Xanten', accepted in 1666), to France in 1807 (Tilsit), to the Grand Duchy of Berg in 1808 and to Prussia in 1815.

capitals.name: Hamm
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Hamm'; Hamm was 'founded by his son Adolf I, Count of the Mark in 1226'.

correction.text: the County of Mark between the Ruhr and the Lippe, about 3,000 km2

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Mark row). The page: 'The County of Mark enclosed an area of approximately 3,000 km2'. A 31 km circle at 7.55E 51.52N (about 3,000 km2, the circle duchy-of-cleves uses for the 1391 gain) is a soft stand-in. The page says 'new territories in the north (Higher Mark) were gained during the 14th century in wars against the Prince-Bishopric of Münster', undated, so the outline is not stepped.

ledger.note: 1160: Berg-Altena. 'The territory emerged under the name of Berg-Altena in 1160' (infobox 'Established: 12th century'); About 1198 Count Frederick I purchased the Mark Oberhof.

The 1220s: Burg Mark near Hamm. The seat 'moved to Burg Mark near Hamm in the 1220s'; Hamm was 'founded by his son Adolf I, Count of the Mark in 1226'. Entered at 1226 as the only year the page gives.

1391: Cleves-Mark. 'In 1391, Adolph III also inherited the Mark from his elder brother Engelbert III' (Adolph had 'acquired the County of Cleves ... in 1368'); he 'united both counties as Cleves-Mark in 1394'.

wars.name: Battle of Worringen

zones.text: the Mark and the lower Rhine round Worringen

wars.outcome: 'Count Eberhard II fought on the side of Duke John I of Brabant'; afterward 'the county gained supremacy in southern Westphalia'.
wars.note: Guelders as the opponent follows the Berg page (Adolf VIII of Berg fought 'against Guelders in 1288'); this page names only Brabant's side.

certainty.note: The page gives an area (about 3,000 km2) and no boundary; the northern gains of the 14th century are undated.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Mark row.

SCOPE. 1160 to 1391. From 1368 the Count of the Mark also held Cleves (personal union, rule 4); after 1391 the Mark is inside duchy-of-cleves (dissolves 1614 into electorate-of-brandenburg per that dossier). The page also dates: 1807 Tilsit (Mark to France), 1808 Grand Duchy of Berg, 'To Prussia: 1815'. The 1444-1449 Soest feud and the dates of Unna, Iserlohn, Luenen, Hoerde, Luedenscheid and Wetter are not on the page.

SHAPE. 31 km circle at 7.55E 51.52N. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Hamm', 'Altena', 'Unna', 'Iserlohn'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The Higher Mark gained from Münster in the 14th century (undated); (2) the 1226 capital move is confidence 1; (3) the Worringen opponent is taken from the Berg page.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new.
